correctness.rationale: One fixed cyclotomic 10-tangent input is defined over Q(zeta5), and the supplied independent-from-tables standard-library checker reconstructs all 61 output lines from exactly 45 seed crossings. It groups all 1830 pair intersections as 551 geometric points, verifies pair-incidence identity and the 7/20/524 Galois orbit degrees. Primitive integral lines have no simultaneous zero coefficients modulo any prime. Exact enumeration of 35,990 line triples has 2,060 zero determinants and 33,930 nonzero determinants whose algebraic norms have precisely prime support {2,3,5,11,19}; this proves universal lattice stability outside that set. Exhaustive finite-field arithmetic for the five exceptional primes yields all component counts, geometric incidence histograms and Frobenius-fixed point totals; it is exhaustive for those concrete finite cases. Uniform Frobenius counts and prime densities follow via C4 action and Dirichlet. These are exact algorithms with transparent finite bounds and explicit checked certificates, not experimental extrapolation. The real/complex regular-decagon identification comes from the ten conic tangents. Boundaries and model dependence are stated.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of the construction and its closest matroid/operator predecessor found the complex 61-line construction and its characteristic-zero data to be pre-existing. The narrowly claimed result is instead the full arithmetic specialization of a specified integral cyclotomic model: all five exceptional reductions, an infinite-prime determinant norm obstruction, and the complete rational singular-support spectrum. These do not follow from complex freeness or point multiplicity tables alone. Searches in mathematical-record and published literature returned no equivalent theorem, with residual risk from unindexed ancillary computations. A failed database search is not itself a novelty proof.

value.rationale: The regular-decagon O61 arrangement is a distinguished rigid, free 61-line geometric object. The complete arithmetic boundary of its natural integral cyclotomic tangent presentation is mathematically motivated: exact disappearance/coalescence primes 2,3,5,11,19 and complete incidence strata at all five, plus a global guarantee at every other prime. The Galois orbit counts give a nontrivial, explicit arithmetic point-count function, including sharp 7/27/551 residue-class behavior, rather than an arbitrary finite snapshot. This precision can guide arithmetic realizations, modular incidence computations and comparisons with alternative models. The model relative nature reduces but does not erase the concrete value of the canonical tangent-coordinate arithmetic classification; known complex freeness and multiplicity data are not given novelty credit.
